key_risks.title: Cloud SLA ≠ NESO curtailment
key_risks.body: Parametrix's four disclosed non-damage products (trigger gap 0/4) pay on cloud-provider SLA and availability-index triggers, not NESO gate status or distribution curtailment orders. UK DC cedants hedged on Parametrix downtime cover may still face basis risk when grid-firmness losses lack an insurable outage event — the MGA monitors 750+ data centres on provider telemetry, not constraint-register curtailment.

key_risks.title: Three-zone DC asset correlation
key_risks.body: Register-derived aggregation scores 4/4: MW-weighted HHI 0.3333 across three linked UK assets (Kao Harlow, Ark, Latos Bridgend) spanning east England, south-west and south Wales boundary zones. A correlated regional grid or cloud outage can trigger concurrent SLA claims on the specialist DC book — Parametrix Analytics models outage correlation on proprietary data, but linked-asset concentration exceeds typical diversified carrier books.

key_risks.title: Coverholder capacity opaque
key_risks.body: Lloyd's coverholder backed by A-rated insurers (capital 3/4) but precise aggregate capacity is not publicly disclosed. Book concentration 4/4 on DC/cloud availability means a correlated outage year could exhaust delegated limits before reinsurance responds — close via sfcr_mining on backing syndicates.

key_risks.title: Provisional DC franchise
key_risks.body: 0% filing-backed sub-factor weight — fully assessed profile. Top weighted lines: book concentration 3/4 (Digital Infrastructure Protector, Apr 2026), non-firm intensity 2/4 on grid-connected renewables, data monitoring 3/4. Close via register_pull on UK DC cedant connection status and trigger_mining on Protector wordings.

key_risks.title: Protector lacks curtailment trigger
key_risks.body: Digital Infrastructure Protector integrates construction-plus-operations cover (product fit 3/4) but no dedicated non-firm curtailment or availability product is evidenced — trigger gap 2/4. Standard physical-damage-led placements on power/utilities and DC clients leave basis risk when grid-connection losses lack insurable damage, lagging Marsh Nimbus on quantified dedicated capacity.

key_risks.title: DC-renewable book correlation
key_risks.body: Combined digital-infrastructure and renewable books correlate to constrained-grid regions (aggregation 2/4), partially offset by 140+ country footprint. UK solar-to-SMR supply chains and DC power dependencies share regional grid stress — several cedants could loss-hit concurrently without appearing in broker-level accumulation monitoring.

key_risks.title: Parametric-native, UK non-firm
key_risks.body: Skyline's four disclosed non-damage parametric products (trigger gap 0/4, product fit 4/4) directly address grid and weather-driven business interruption — the opposite of legacy physical-damage BI. Non-firm intensity 3/4 reflects explicit interruptible-power exposure on the UK parametric franchise; data monitoring 4/4 supports index-linked triggers.

key_risks.title: Five-year cover, three-year history
key_risks.body: Disclosed max cover tenor T=5.0y against claims history H=3.0y yields tenor mismatch index m=0.133 (rating 2/4). Longer parametric programmes on evolving UK constraint zones outrun the empirical loss record — pricing on grid-index triggers may understate tail scenarios as NESO constraint costs escalate.

key_risks.title: Portfolio proxy HHI 0.93
key_risks.body: Register-derived aggregation scores 3/4: MW-weighted HHI 0.9348 over 46 mapped L3 assets across six boundary zones. Correlated parametric triggers in east England and Scotland constraint areas can activate multiple policies simultaneously — book concentration stays moderate at 2/4 but geographic index correlation concentrates tail risk.

key_risks.title: Provisional wholesale broker
key_risks.body: 0% filing-backed sub-factor weight — fully assessed profile. Top weighted lines: book concentration 3/4 on energy and construction, non-firm intensity 2/4, underwriting expertise 3/4. Close via register_pull on UK power cedant placements and trigger_mining on energy programme wordings.

key_risks.title: Indemnity-led energy placement
key_risks.body: Trigger gap 2/4 and product fit 2/4 — Price Forbes places traditional indemnity energy and engineering cover without an evidenced parametric or availability desk. Curtailment and non-damage BI losses on UK renewable and power clients may fall outside primary wordings placed through the Ardonagh wholesale book.

key_risks.title: Broking analytics gap
key_risks.body: Data monitoring and pricing modelling both score 2/4 — credible wholesale capability without register-linked curtailment analytics or constraint-index monitoring. Energy placements rely on carrier wordings and client engineering data rather than NESO telemetry — close via entity_analysis on operational BI endorsements.

key_risks.title: Fifteen-year cover, three-year data
key_risks.body: Standout tenor mismatch 4/4: disclosed max cover tenor T=15.0y vs claims history H=3.0y yields m=0.800 — batch maximum among energy MGAs. UK renewable and battery projects with multi-decade asset lives sit on covers whose empirical loss record spans only three years; grid-connection timeline evolution outruns pricing credibility.

key_risks.title: Two parametric lines only
key_risks.body: Disclosed n=2 non-damage products → trigger gap 2/4 and product fit 2/4. NER underwrites construction and operational risk for UK renewables via Paragon/AXA XL backing, but curtailment and availability without physical damage likely fall outside the two evidenced parametric lines — indemnity structures dominate the specialist book.

key_risks.title: Exposure meets preparedness
key_risks.body: Earning-it quadrant with margin of safety −1.0 — exposure 71.0 vs preparedness 70.0. Book concentration 3/4 on UK renewable construction/operational phases drives exposure; AXA XL/Paragon capacity (3/4) and underwriting expertise (3/4) provide credible infrastructure but do not close the tenor and trigger gaps on non-firm grid events.

key_risks.title: Exposure outruns tooling
key_risks.body: Exposed quadrant — margin of safety −32.1 with exposure 72.1 vs preparedness 40.0. Book concentration 3/4 and non-firm intensity 3/4 on wind, solar and BESS portfolios collide with data monitoring 1/4 and pricing modelling 1/4 — batch-low analytics for an energy specialist facing first-order grid curtailment risk.

key_risks.title: One non-damage product
key_risks.body: Disclosed n=1 non-damage product → trigger gap 3/4 and product fit 1/4. Renewable Guard's indemnity-led renewable covers leave curtailment and availability losses without dedicated parametric triggers — basis risk persists on UK merchant wind and BESS portfolios where grid-connection uncertainty is a first-order peril.

key_risks.title: Portfolio zone concentration
key_risks.body: Register-derived aggregation 3/4: HHI 0.9348 over 46 mapped L3 assets across six UK boundary zones. Correlated constraint events in shared renewable geographies can hit multiple cedants on the specialist book simultaneously — aggregation models on indemnity wordings may not capture register-linked curtailment correlation.

key_risks.title: Flood index, not grid NFRI
key_risks.body: Previsico's two disclosed non-damage products (trigger gap 2/4) trigger on hydrological flood forecasts and sensor-verified depth — not NESO gate status or distribution curtailment. Book concentration 1/4 confirms peripheral NFRI relevance: strong parametric monitoring 4/4 on flood perils does not extend to UK power or DC grid-availability indices.

key_risks.title: Platform, not underwriter
key_risks.body: Underwriting expertise 0/4 and capital/reinsurance 1/4 — Previsico supplies flood models and triggers to partner carriers rather than holding risk on its own balance sheet. Pricing modelling 3/4 on hydrological perils outpaces the entity's direct underwriting authority; NFRI curtailment placements require carrier wordings Previsico does not control.

key_risks.title: Correlated flood footprints
key_risks.body: Aggregation correlation 3/4 on shared catchment geographies — a major UK flood event triggers multiple sensor-linked policies simultaneously. This is peril-specific clustering distinct from grid-node correlation; non-firm intensity effective rating 0/4 confirms no interruptible-power book despite portfolio HHI 0.9348 on the L3 proxy.

key_risks.title: US cat, not UK grid
key_risks.body: Book concentration 1/4 and non-firm intensity 1/4 confirm Vave sits outside the core UK non-firm power cohort — algorithmic commercial property and homeowners dominate. Aggregation correlation 3/4 reflects Atlantic seaboard hurricane geography, not NESO constraint zones; NFRI relevance is limited to nascent parametric extensions.

key_risks.title: Weather modules, not curtailment
key_risks.body: Two disclosed non-damage products — instant-bind algorithmic property and parametric-adjacent weather peril modules (trigger gap 2/4) — address US commercial property extremes, not UK availability-index or curtailment BI. Product fit 2/4: tech-forward underwriting (800+ data fields, data monitoring 4/4) does not translate to grid-firmness triggers.

key_risks.title: Delegated-authority capacity
key_risks.body: Capital/reinsurance 1/4 — Acrisure-acquired delegated-authority MGA reliant on carrier capacity rather than balance-sheet underwriting. Algorithmic pricing engine (3/4) scales US property quoting but UK DC or power cedant participation is not evidenced on the product pages.

key_risks.title: Storm grid-loss, not curtailment
key_risks.body: Raincoat's power-grid income parametric pays when storms destroy grid infrastructure (trigger gap 0/4 across four disclosed products) — availability-style exposure at non-firm intensity 2/4. Basis risk remains vs NESO constraint-indexed curtailment: parametric triggers on catastrophe grid destruction differ from orderly non-firm connection curtailment without physical damage.

key_risks.title: Cat geography clustering
key_risks.body: Hurricane and earthquake index products drive aggregation correlation 3/4 on shared catastrophe geographies. A regional hurricane event can activate grid-loss, flood and wind parametrics concurrently across Raincoat's platform — correlated nat-cat triggers concentrate tail beyond individual policy limits.

key_risks.title: Partner-carrier risk transfer
key_risks.body: Capital/reinsurance 1/4 — venture-backed platform supplying parametric models and distribution to partner insurers rather than holding underwriting capital. Real-time disaster monitoring (4/4) and product fit (4/4) exceed balance-sheet capacity; UK non-firm power scale depends on reinsurer appetite behind the platform.

key_risks.title: BI endorsements only
key_risks.body: One disclosed non-damage product — renewable energy specialty line with non-damage BI endorsements — yields trigger gap 3/4 and product fit 1/4. Optio's diversified specialty platform places traditional indemnity cover across niche lines; curtailment and availability without physical damage likely fall outside the single evidenced endorsement on the renewable line.

key_risks.title: Breadth over grid concentration
key_risks.body: Book concentration 1/4, non-firm intensity 1/4 and aggregation correlation 1/4 — Optio's strength is specialty breadth, not grid-interruptible concentration. European renewable-energy expansion adds sector relevance but the book remains below index median exposure; energy acquisitions have not yet shifted register-linked non-firm intensity.

key_risks.title: No curtailment analytics
key_risks.body: Pricing modelling 1/4 and data monitoring 2/4 — no published methodology or register-linked monitoring beyond standard specialty underwriting. Underwriting expertise 3/4 on complex risks does not compensate for absent parametric or constraint-index tooling on the renewable line; delegated-authority capital 1/4 limits product innovation scope.

Margin of safety −17.6 reflects clients exposed to non-firm perils through indemnity structures while the AUB Group broker lacks differentiated monitoring or parametric product capability.

key_risks.title: Zero non-damage products
key_risks.body: Disclosed n=0 non-damage products → trigger gap 4/4 and product fit 0/4 — batch maximum basis-risk gap among carriers. Syndicate 1225's utility property and conventional power underwriting relies on physical-damage-led wordings; curtailment and availability without insurable damage leave UK energy cedants on legacy BI structures vs Parametrix or Skyline parametric peers.

key_risks.title: Utility mutual depth, 2% energy GWP
key_risks.body: Disclosed energy/power GWP share 2.4% (£24.09m of £1,011.5m) keeps book concentration 1/4 at syndicate level, but parent AEGIS is a utility mutual with deep named bench including ex-LMA Power Generation Panel leadership. Non-firm intensity 2/4 (propagated) and engineering-led utility property assessment may underweight register-linked curtailment on the small but expert energy slice.

key_risks.title: A+ capital, no grid telemetry
key_risks.body: A+ FSR (capital 4/4) provides ample margin-of-safety 1.5, but data monitoring 2/4 reflects Opal/Digital Lead-Follow platform digitisation rather than asset-level grid telemetry or curtailment monitoring. Five-year max cover vs three-year claims history (tenor mismatch 2/4) on utility property outruns empirical curtailment loss data — close via register_pull on UK cedant connection status.
